name: Globe and Mail cryptic crossword No 3,339

blocks.note: Ian is the stock Scottish first name

explanation.surface: A courteous Scot who has never served in the army.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma makes 'no soldier' look like a further description of the Scotsman; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain definition by negation: anyone outside the armed forces is a civilian.

clue.text: Can try entrée, specially cooked for anniversary

indicators.note: cooking reworks raw ingredients into a new dish, just as the letters are reworked into a new word

explanation.surface: A suggestion to sample a specially prepared main course at an anniversary dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: The kitchen talk makes 'entrée' look like food; it is only letters, and the accent drops.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by class: the three-hundredth year after an event is one particular kind of anniversary.

blocks.note: an end = an aim or target, as in 'ends and means'
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A golfer noting that the target is near at hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close' reads as the adjective 'near'; it is the noun (rhyming with 'rose'), the close of a day or story.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym once 'close' is read as the noun: the close of a film is its final part.

blocks.note: pa = dad, with the possessive S kept
a tit is a small songbird, such as the blue tit

explanation.surface: A father's pet bird is getting on in years.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive S is easy to discard as grammar; here it is a letter the answer needs.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal idiom: someone no longer up to what they once did because of age is said to be past it.

clue.text: No more than 1000 degrees on a regular basis

indicators.note: something done on a regular basis happens at fixed intervals, so take letters at a fixed interval: every second one

blocks.note: M is the Roman numeral for 1000

explanation.surface: A temperature that never exceeds a thousand degrees.
explanation.walkthrough: The numbers suggest a thermometer, but 1000 is a Roman numeral and 'degrees' supplies only its alternate letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: 'a mere child' is no more than a child.

clue.text: Behind farm animal, one trembling bird

indicators.note: what comes behind something follows it, so the second piece is placed after the first
a trembling thing shakes, and shaking jumbles the letters of ONE

blocks.note: a pig is a farm animal

explanation.surface: A nervous bird hiding behind a farmyard beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trembling bird' looks like one unit; 'trembling' belongs with 'one', and 'bird' stands alone as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by class: the familiar city pavement species is one kind of bird.

clue.text: Demonstrator (not male) who takes a bow

indicators.note: 'not male' says the male letter is not to be there, so it comes out

blocks.note: M = male, removed from the front

explanation.surface: A protester who, not being a man, steps forward to take a bow on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Takes a bow' suggests applause; here the bow is the weapon that shoots arrows.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic-leaning description: 'takes a bow' is read literally, as picking up the weapon rather than acknowledging applause.

clue.text: Deception not lasting long for one of my age

blocks.note: a con = a deception, a confidence trick

explanation.surface: A short-lived trick played on someone of the speaker's generation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My age' sounds like a complaint about getting old; it means one's own generation.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain definition: a person born or living in the same period as another.

indicators.note: 'half' asks for half of the word it governs, here the first four of its eight letters

blocks.note: disclose = reveal; keep its front half

explanation.surface: An instruction to expose only half of a written account.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Record' looks like a document to reveal; it is a vinyl record, and DISCLOSE loses its back half, LOSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a gramophone record is a flat round platter.

blocks.note: in = at home, as in 'staying in'

explanation.surface: Someone cared for the woman they are about to marry while she was at home.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a noun here, not the past tense of 'intend': one's intended is the person one means to marry.
explanation.definitionFit: A slightly old-fashioned idiom: the person you are engaged to is 'your intended'.

blocks.note: reads like a number or a grade; it is a time, twelve o'clock at night
reads like a mark or a size; it asks what a single G describes, and G is the middle of the five-letter word for the dark hours

explanation.surface: A puzzling note about a grade or a size marked 12G.
explanation.walkthrough: Twelve is the time; G sits at the centre of NIGHT, so the answer describes the letter as well as the hour.
explanation.definitionFit: Both readings hold: twelve at night is the hour, and 'mid-night' names where G sits in NIGHT.

clue.text: Who moved, and in what manner?

indicators.note: letters that are moved change places, so WHO is rearranged

explanation.surface: A reporter's questions: who moved, and how did they do it?
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a list of journalist's questions, and the answer is another of them.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the question word asking about manner or method.

indicators.note: an area is a part of a larger place, so the answer is one part of the city's name

explanation.surface: A rough neighbourhood of the Spanish city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal area' reads as a district with a crime problem; the break falls after 'Criminal'.
explanation.definitionFit: A near synonym: both words describe wicked, morally wrong acts.

clue.text: Naive pope — one of an unlucky number

definitions.text: pope — one of an unlucky number

blocks.clueFragment: pope — one of an unlucky number
blocks.note: a papal name held by thirteen popes

explanation.surface: A gullible pontiff who belongs to an ill-starred line.
explanation.walkthrough: The unlucky number is thirteen: there have been thirteen popes named Innocent.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: naive means lacking worldly experience, and the pope sense is a regnal name.

clue.text: I’m frightened about receiving new joint

indicators.note: to turn about is to face the other way, so the word is reversed
a word receiving a letter takes it inside itself

blocks.note: eek! is a cry of fright; turned about it is KEE

explanation.surface: A patient nervous about having a replacement joint fitted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like 'concerning', but it reverses the cry of fright.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the leg's middle hinge is one kind of joint.

blocks.note: broad, wide-ranging, as in a generalisation
clearing a floor with a broom

explanation.surface: An army general reduced to housework.
explanation.walkthrough: 'General' looks like an officer; it is the adjective meaning broad, as in a sweeping statement.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: an adjective for wide-ranging claims, and the present participle of the broom chore.

indicators.note: a coat is what covers the outside, so take only the outer letters

explanation.surface: A leftover fur coat that no one wants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fur coat' reads as one garment; 'coat' belongs with 'nobody'. 'Spare' is the adjective meaning lean.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a spare figure carries no extra flesh.

clue.text: Several scores of great significance, but not initially

indicators.note: 'not initially' means 'except at the start', so the word loses its first letter

blocks.note: weighty = of great significance; its W goes

explanation.surface: Musical scores that would matter, except at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scores' suggests sheet music or results; a score is twenty.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by arithmetic: four scores of twenty make the number, and four counts as several.

blocks.note: Pl. is the street-name abbreviation for Place

explanation.surface: A pleasant spot where the pressure is letting up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Place' is not a location here but an abbreviation, as used on street signs.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both adjectives describe what gives pleasure or contentment.

blocks.note: David ___, director of Lawrence of Arabia

explanation.surface: A slim, fit British movie director.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface runs the two senses together as a single person: David Lean directed Lawrence of Arabia and Brief Encounter.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: the adjective for a trim, fat-free build, and the surname of the director.

clue.text: One of three English kings missing a way of great worth

indicators.note: a word missing something lacks it, so the named letters are taken out

blocks.note: England had kings Richard I, II and III

explanation.surface: A monarch who lacks a route to riches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Way' is a road, shortened as on a street sign; with it and 'a' gone from the end, the king keeps only his first four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a rich prize or rich deposit is one of great value.

explanation.surface: Stuffing oneself from a can over on the other side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gorge' looks like the verb 'eat greedily'; it is the noun, a ravine.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both nouns name a deep, steep-sided valley cut by a river.

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its ends, so take the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A drunken despot delivering a raving address.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both name an absolute ruler who governs cruelly.
